scenario: new investor, worried, Roth income limit

turns.text: I put $7,500 in my Roth in January and I think my income might be too high this year. What happens now?

It depends on how far over the limit you land, and there are only three outcomes.

Under the phase-out range: nothing happens, the contribution stands.

Inside the phase-out range: part of the $7,500 is allowed and the rest is an excess contribution. You'd withdraw the excess plus the earnings on it before your filing deadline, including extensions.

Above the range: none of it is allowed. Same fix for the whole $7,500, or you recharacterize it to a traditional IRA instead, which keeps the money invested and avoids pulling it out.

If you leave an excess in past the deadline it's a 6% penalty for each year it stays. You have until April 2027 with extensions, so there's time — you'll know which case you're in once your income is final.
